summary: Red Island Light: a stone tower of 1848 on a reef-bound islet in the St. Lawrence opposite the Saguenay mouth. Automated in 1988; now a bird refuge.

lens.note: original 1848 apparatus of 24 oil lamps and reflectors; the 1890 and 1916 changes are in events

structures.note: masonry tower; 20.1 m to the top of the lantern

access.note: Reached only by boat. Tower closed. Island within the Saguenay-St. Lawrence Marine Park and a bird refuge.

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (Fisheries and Oceans Canada)

events.note: Tower built 1847 to 1848 by Joseph Archer to a contract of 20 February 1847.
Red Island lightship moored northeast of the island; the bulletin gives 9 July 1871 as the first light, LighthouseFriends gives 1 July 1871 for the mooring.
Fixed red light replaced by a white flashing light, turned by a weight-driven mechanism.
Quadruple long-focus reflector installed; the flash signature changed again.
Diaphone fog signal: a two-second blast, then twenty-eight seconds of silence.
Radiobeacon installed. The chronology gives 1945; the article text says the year after Gilbert Fraser's first season.
Electronic fog detection with loudspeakers replaced the manned fog horn.
The 1850 keeper's house replaced by two new houses.
Kerosene burner replaced by an electric lamp, supplied by diesel generators.
Light automated; the last keepers left Red Island.
CIMEVIR interpretation centre created to restore the buildings.
Radiobeacon closed and a new light system installed.
First visitors to the keepers' houses under the CIMEVIR venture.
Visitor venture ended after the 2000 season.
Government announced that all buildings except the light would be destroyed; a 2019 tender followed.

keepers.name: Augustin Dufour
keepers.note: First keeper. Trained on Île Verte; resigned in December 1848 and returned in January 1849. LighthouseFriends gives 1848 to 1850.

keepers.name: Walter
keepers.note: Named in the bulletin by surname only; left in charge with Nicolas Pelletier in December 1848.

keepers.name: Nicolas Pelletier
keepers.note: A young man left in charge with Walter when Dufour left the island, December 1848.

keepers.name: Gilbert Lindsay
keepers.note: Went out to the island with Smith and Drysdale in November 1848; fell ill and left by the end of that month.

keepers.name: Gilbert Lindsay
keepers.note: The bulletin has him leave for Île Verte after 1861; LighthouseFriends gives 1860 to 1867 at Red Island.

other_stations.name: Île Verte lighthouse
other_stations.note: Followed his father, Robert Noël Lindsay, to Île Verte in 1867.

keepers.name: Hubert Fraser
keepers.note: Drowned with his son Daniel on 11 October 1860, on a supply trip to the south shore.

keepers.name: Daniel Fraser
keepers.note: Son of Hubert Fraser; drowned with him on 11 October 1860, aged 22.

keepers.name: Pierre-Elzéar Fraser
keepers.note: Fourth keeper; succeeded Gilbert Lindsay. LighthouseFriends gives 1867 to 1889. Died in December 1889.

keepers.name: Alfred Côté
keepers.note: Ran the light alone for about two weeks in December 1889 while the keeper was ill.

keepers.name: Pierre-Théodore Fraser
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends gives 1889 as his start. Married Angèle Caroline Lindsay in 1891. Retired in 1927.

keepers.name: Théobald Fraser
keepers.note: Came from Île Verte. LighthouseFriends lists T. Fraser from 1927 to at least 1937.

keepers.name: Gilbert Fraser
keepers.note: Veteran wounded in Normandy in 1944. Moved to Cap-de-Bon-Désir in 1958. LighthouseFriends lists him at least 1952.

keepers.name: Armand Lafrance
keepers.note: Began as an assistant on Île Verte in 1951, then worked under Gilbert Fraser at Red Island. The bulletin gives no dates for his Red Island years.

keepers.name: Maurice Thibault
keepers.note: Left after the 1959 holiday season.

keepers.name: Patrice Thibault
keepers.note: Appointed assistant the same month as his brother; the bulletin gives no end date for this stint.

keepers.name: Patrice Thibault
keepers.note: Second-crew keeper (gardien surveillant).

keepers.name: Patrice Thibault
keepers.note: Principal keeper; resigned in 1987.

keepers.name: Antoine Therrien
keepers.note: Came from the Île Blanche pillar; left the station in 1978, aged 65.

keepers.name: Joseph Lévesque
keepers.note: Master of the Red Island lightship; drowned on 16 October 1876, crossing from the shore to his ship.

keepers.name: David Levesque
keepers.note: Brother of Joseph Lévesque; took command for the rest of the 1876 season.

keepers.name: Silvio Petitgrew
keepers.note: Master of the lightship from 1898; drowned on 9 September 1899.

wrecks.outcome: Waterlogged and abandoned; pushed onto the reef by ice; refloated by Hubert Fraser and his sons; taken to Tadoussac.
Lost on the reef in a snowstorm; thirteen men left in a boat and were lost; the ship was lightened, freed and reached Quebec on 14 June.
Driven onto the reef in a gale with timber; freed with help from the lightship's master, Joseph Lévesque.
Aground near the light with livestock and rails; the captain and two officers stayed aboard until the tug Lord Stanley rescued them.
Struck Red Island shoal while towing a barge; temporary repairs at Quebec, then dry dock at Halifax.
Ashore on Red Island Reef; pilot's certificate suspended for eighteen months.
Destroyed in a storm; all hands lost.
Aground on the reef in fog; the pilot was fined one hundred dollars and the master admonished.
Pushed onto the reef by the bœuf current after leaving the Saguenay.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The bulletin gives 11 November 1848 (citing the Journal de Québec of 30 November 1848); LighthouseFriends says late 1848; the Lighthouse Directory says 1848. The story uses 1848 and the 11 November date.

The bulletin and the Québec record give a 15.5 m masonry tower and a 20.1 m total with the lantern; the Lighthouse Directory gives 19.5 m for the tower; the Coast Guard list gives a 20.1 m focal height. The brief's 20.1 m is the total height.
The bulletin dates the brick-and-wood keeper's house to 1850; the Québec record says the first house was of 1848. Both say its replacement came in 1965.

LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory name the Canadian Coast Guard as owner; the bulletin names Fisheries and Oceans Canada. The Coast Guard is part of Fisheries and Oceans Canada, so the page names both.
LighthouseFriends dates the lightship's mooring to 1 July 1871; the bulletin gives 9 July 1871 as the day her light first showed. The story gives both dates.

The bulletin names a 20-year-old Gilbert Lindsay of Île Verte as the 1848 assistant (pp. 28-29), and separately a son of the Île Verte keeper Robert-Noël Lindsay who was keeper at Red Island in 1860-61 (p. 30). It does not say they are the same man; LighthouseFriends gives Red Island 1860-1867. The roster keeps two lines and the story does not link them.

notes_for_editor: Verified 2026-10-27 against the bulletin's own page footers (page N ends each printed page), the Coast Guard List of Lights (entry 1770), the Rowlett directory (qcc.htm), LighthouseFriends (ID 1625), the Amis des phares page, the Quebec heritage record, and the Marine reports read from the Internet Archive text (1902 volume, 1903, 1906, 1908 and 1909 volumes). Corrections made: units (metres first for the 1847 excavation depths and the reflectors); the Lindsay identity (the 1848 assistant and the 1860-61 keeper are not linked by any source, so the story no longer says they are the same man); the lightship first-light date (conflict now stated); the Pride of Canada crew (the bulletin says the thirteen men perished); the Lafrance paraphrase; the 1873 ice detail ('over the ice' replaced by LighthouseFriends' 'through ice to the south shore'); the Montrose court wording now follows the court ('continued at full speed, and on too fine a course'); the fence wording now follows the 177-page specification (a fence to limit access, purpose: warn visitors of falling debris); the CIMEVIR wording ('restore' is the bulletin's stated first task); the venture ended wording; the owner conflict (Fisheries and Oceans Canada per the bulletin; Canadian Coast Guard per the Coast Guard directory and LighthouseFriends); the Friends of Lighthouses name changed to Amis des phares; 'the tower is not open for climbing' changed to 'closed to visitors' (the sources say tower closed). Two footnotes corrected: [^14] split to [^14][^16] for the 1848 light and Lindsay's age (page 28); [^33] now gives the scan page (110) with printed page 101 from the corpus. A new footnote [^45] (bulletin p. 13) supports the islet and reef description. Open items: (1) the bulletin's 1848 Gilbert Lindsay and the 1860 keeper may be the same man; no source says so. (2) The Iberian footnote [^31] has only the scan page (54); the printed page is not confirmed. (3) Gilbert Lindsay's move to Île Verte in 1867 is given by both the bulletin and LighthouseFriends; LighthouseFriends' Red Island dates (1860-1867) are kept as a stated difference from the bulletin's 1861. (4) Living people: Luc Caron (last keeper at the Prince Shoal light), Patrice Thibault and Antoine Therrien (service ended 1978-1987), Armand Lafrance, and Charles-Hector Fraser are named only as the bulletin prints them, in their public roles; personal details are the bulletin's own. (5) The brief's 20.1 m is the total height with the lantern; the Coast Guard focal height is also 20.1 m. (6) No rows of OCR tables are relied on in this station's story.
